interactions.summary: Jiang says private Bible reading in Dante's historical world would be treated as sinful because unsupervised interpretation exposed the reader to confusion and satanic distortion.
A student asks whether Dante's coin metaphor, anti-church pressure, and nonliteral reading of scripture make him a precursor to Protestantism or later heretical movements.
Jiang answers with maximal scope, saying his class argument is that Dante inspired not only the Reformation but the Renaissance, the age of revolution, the Enlightenment, and modernity itself.
A student reads Dante's formal answer to Peter: belief in one God who moves the heavens by love, supported by physical and metaphysical proofs as well as by scriptural revelation.
Jiang reframes the issue by asking why 'God is love' would be heretical for the Church, rejects a student's moral reading, and insists that the problem is formal divergence from required doctrine.

claims.claim: Jiang says that in Dante's historical setting, reading the Bible alone would be treated as sinful because solitary interpretation could be confused by satanic suggestion.
He says his class argument is that Dante inspired everything from Protestant reform through the Renaissance, revolution, Enlightenment, and modernity itself.
The quoted passage has Dante declare belief in one eternal God who motionlessly moves the heavens by love and grounds that belief in physical proofs, metaphysical proofs, and scriptural revelation.
claims.temporal_scope: Claim inside the text being read on 2026-06-18.

claims.claim: Jiang interprets the exam scene as forcing Dante to state what he believes about God, and he foregrounds Dante's answer that God is love.
He argues that for the Catholic Church the problem is not the phrase 'one God' but the fact that Dante does not simply recite the required doctrinal formula and instead says 'God is love.'

signature_moments.moment: Jiang answers a narrow historical question by declaring Dante the source not only of Protestant reform but of modernity itself.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the lecture's largest ambition claims and shows how total Jiang's genealogy of Dante becomes.

signature_moments.moment: Dante answers a doctrinal exam not with a creed formula but with the claim that the unmoved mover is love.
signature_moments.source_phrase: I believe that God is love
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the hinge that lets Jiang recast the whole exchange as both theological compression and latent heresy.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The quoted Dante passage says faith in God is supported not only by scripture but also by natural and philosophical forms of proof.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang stretches Dante's influence forward across later historical eras, explicitly linking this medieval scene to the Reformation, Renaissance, Enlightenment, and modernity as downstream developments.

uncertainty_notes.note: Jiang presents Dante's total civilizational influence as his own class argument rather than as a demonstrated historical consensus, so preserve the sweep but not as a settled factual genealogy.
